Estimate Distributions Using Statistical Decision Guidance

Source: R/stats.R
estimate_distribution.Rd

Estimates an appropriate distributional model for each group using censoring-aware statistical decision rules.

Usage

estimate_distribution(
  df,
  distribution_config = "auto",
  result_col = analysis_result_var(df)
)

Arguments

df

Grouped data frame or `env_schema` object.

distribution_config

Configuration list supplied to distribution fitting functions.

If `"auto"` (the default), configuration settings are obtained from the group's [statistical_decision()] object.

Value

A tibble containing one row per group.

The returned table includes statistical decision metadata together with the distribution evaluation result.

n_detect

Number of non-censored observations.

percent_censored

Percentage of observations classified as censored.

censoring_class

Censoring classification used for method selection.

distribution_method

Recommended distribution estimation approach.

trend_method

Recommended trend evaluation method.

trend_guidance

Recommended interpretation of trend analyses.

censored_method

Recommended censored-data handling method.

distribution_config

Distribution-fitting configuration used during evaluation. This is a named list of arguments passed to [EnvStats::distChoose()] or [EnvStats::distChooseCensored()].

interval_config

Recommended interval estimation settings.

decision_basis

Basis used to select the statistical approach.

distribution

Selected distribution or recommended distributional approach.

n_used

Number of observations used during evaluation.

result

Distribution fitting result object.

Details

`estimate_distribution()` automatically evaluates the percentage of censored observations and available sample size using [derive_decision()]. A [statistical_decision()] object is then used to select the recommended distribution estimation pathway for each group.

Depending on the degree of censoring, groups are evaluated using:

  • `"parametric"` distribution fitting

  • `"ros_censored"` censored distribution fitting

  • `"nonparametric"` distribution classification

  • `"descriptive_only"` evaluation

  • `"insufficient_data"` when too few observations are available

Distribution fitting is performed independently within each group and requires the input data to already be grouped using [dplyr::group_by()].

Method selection follows the active guidance profile used by [statistical_decision()].

Under the default EPA-style guidance:

ConditionRecommendationAction
n_used < 4insufficient_datano distribution fitting
<15% censoredparametricfit candidate distributions
15-50% censoredros_censoredcensored distribution fitting
50-90% censorednonparametricclassify as nonparametric
>=90% censoreddescriptive_onlydescriptive evaluation only

Parametric evaluations use candidate distributions specified by `distribution_config`, typically through [EnvStats::distChoose()]. By default, distribution fitting evaluates normal and lognormal candidate distributions using the `"sf"` selection method.

Censored evaluations use [EnvStats::distChooseCensored()] with left-censoring assumptions.

Nonparametric and descriptive-only groups do not perform formal distribution fitting and instead return recommendation metadata for downstream analyses.

See also

[statistical_decision()], [derive_decision()], [guidance_profile()], [guidance_options()]

Examples

gw |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    location_id,
    param_name,
    default_unit
  ) |>
  estimate_distribution()
